Roadwarrior (H91)

Region (English scoring table): Serpentspine.

One-line profile: Put a country on an Orcish war convoy, migrate and raid along the underground railways, and tear down the world behind you.

Story: High｜Mission-tree length: Medium (26 direct missions)｜Version: locally supports EU4 v1.37.5.0｜Uniqueness: Extremely high｜Early pressure: High｜Expansion: High, but unlike settled-empire play

A country that cannot quietly hold a city

Roadwarrior is the playable Black Orc warband H91 in 1444. The English offline Wiki's same-name clan entry is chiefly an identity card, and its snapshot does not provide a complete founding history; this article does not invent an ancient dynasty. The current scripts do show that the warband treats the underground road and war machine as its way of survival. The player does not first repair a hold and then rule stable territory; they activate the “Great Convoy,” keep moving along the roads, and survive through combat, raiding and vehicle upgrades. [Local script][Wiki source]

The convoy is not merely a narrative metaphor. Dedicated reforms, decisions, events and missions support a one-province migration rhythm: assemble carriages, accumulate movement resources, launch high-speed marches at the right time, and then absorb cooldown and supply pressure. The strategic question is when to seize the next section of road, what to do with the land behind you, and whether to keep treating the whole mountain range as fuel. Mission rewards and events can leave roads that have been crossed with a long-lasting or permanent loss of normal colonization value; this is not ordinary territorial expansion. [Local script][Local event text]

The road modifier can be checked directly: some missions apply the permanent roadwarrior_decolonized modifier to underground roads. In the current base Mod it reduces local colonial growth by 1000. This proves a severe map consequence, but it does not tell us how many inhabitants a province had or how many people died; those population figures cannot be inferred from the modifier. [Local script]

From convoy to scorched earth

The early story is about turning a loose Orc warband into a mobile community capable of breaking through passes. As the convoy grows, loot and mechanical modifications increase its ability to surge forward, and missions continually push the war into the next stretch of road. Its appeal is the exceptional campaign speed and an extreme resource logic: if a place cannot be held, make it unusable to those who come later. The cost is that stable territory, diplomatic development and long-term construction are deliberately secondary. [Local script]

This country should not be evaluated by the usual standard for a conquest state. Ordinary Orc identity and ordinary warfare are not reasons to reduce its values score; the serious evidence concerns the destructive treatment of residents, roads and habitable environments in missions and events. Script text describes roads being burned into difficult-to-repopulate wasteland, and mission effects write a lasting block on later colonization. The game modifier and the narrative population harm must be described separately; every map change must not be fabricated into a known death toll. [Local script][Local event text]

Settling down is a separate boundary. After meeting conditions, Roadwarrior may settle and turn toward Karashar Z57, but this is an independent later choice, not an automatic successor granted by the H91 mission tree. Nor can we claim that the Great Convoy mechanics remain unchanged after the Tag switch. [Local decision]

How players use it

Treat the campaign as a “railway hunt”: first ensure that the convoy can start and be maintained, then open the underground route section by section through speed, raiding and upgrades. Every move requires decisions about direction, overload cooldown and enemy counterattacks. If you prefer accumulating development, repairing holds and running trade, almost every Roadwarrior policy works against that instinct. Two player posts likewise discuss Greentide-style advance and a later settlement turn, but they are version-specific experiences and cannot prove current script values or an inevitable route. [Community views]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 98/100｜Authoritarianism 83/100｜Magic↔Artifice 35/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 40/100)｜Pluralism 12/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Evil (19/100), with a declining trajectory.

The evidence scope and community links are listed on the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Roadwarrior (H91) — Roadwarrior Ideas

Set ID: H91_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = H91
    }

Roadwarrior Traditions

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Looting speed: +50% (loot_amount; raw value 0.5).

1. Maxug's Madness

Maxug's premonition of becoming the first "Roadwarrior" was compiled into a series of scattered journals, gathered by the Roadcult Book-Engineers in their journey across the Dwarovrod. It detailed Maxug's dreams to devastate the entire Dwarovar, raiding from hold to hold and claiming the many treasures still left by the ancient dwarven empire.

Many orcs from around the Dwarovar joined Maxug’s cause for the promise of loot, but many in turn started to believe in his vision of expanding the great convoy.

  • global_manpower_modifier: +15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

2. Cult of the Road

The Cult of the Road reveres the Dwarovrod itself, seeing it as their domain that they took from the dwarves. With this, they believe that squatters on the roads violate their domain and that they must be stamped out. To maintain our power, new generations must be trained to revere and continue protecting our sacred road.

In our travels, we have discovered many insights on the road as our shamans received visions on its secrets and the many rituals needed to ensure our victory against any intruders daring to defile the holy road.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Embracing Challenge

On the great road we find many enemies, from weak dwarven remnants to occasional giant cave trolls, but everyone we face must die fighting. This tradition is not to preserve our honour or the enemy’s, but rather for us to continue growing stronger, for great rivals have a beauty like none other, and our blades should be tempered with the blood of the strong.

Rather than showing an example to our younger generation which would grow weak fighting unarmed fleeing enemies, we temper their skills in the blood of worthy adversaries.

  • Army tradition: +0.25 (army_tradition; raw value 0.25).

  • Army tradition from battles: +1 (army_tradition_from_battle; raw value 1).

4. Rail Metal

After successful raids, the Roadwarriors would perform large celebrations in the ruins. Many orcs gathered to perform by beating their drums of war and mixing war chants with screams, emulating the screech of metal moving on rails. The festivals often went wild, with the drummers breaking their instruments on stage and throwing themselves off into the crowds.

The music at these festivals was dubbed "Rail Metal" and became very popular after the "artists" perfected their art more and more after successful raids.

  • Stability cost modifier: -10% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.1).

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

5. Thunderdoom

The shamans of the Roadwarrior clan accidentally discovered that channelling lightning magic through the rails of the holy road managed to magically restore them. Using this information, the mages would learn ways to manipulate lightning magic for both offence and to restore broken segments. The most talented of mages managed to entrap enemies into cages made of pure chains of lightning, trapping both orcs and their prey to have a fair fight where no quarter would be given.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

6. Rail Conductors

The orcs not fit to be warriors in the great convoy instead take the role of rail conductors, they navigate the ruins of the Great Road, thus allowing the warriors to reach holds quicker. They maintain the convoy, clear debris on tracks and occasionally scout, allowing our vanguard to easily travel towards new enemies. However, as the conductors do not fight, they take a lower cut of the plunder and are often seen as outcasts to the strongest warriors of the clan.

  • Movement speed: +20% (movement_speed; raw value 0.2).

7. The Sound of Dread

Due to the constant state of war all across the Dwarovar, there were not many permanent settlements made by any of the inhabitants, apart from some remaining dwarven holds. Due to there being little to no unity across the many races, stragglers would often fight for the limited resources and camp in any cave that looked safe enough, but fear would overcome anyone who heard the drums of the Roadwarrior clan.

Booming and echoing across every crevice nearby caves, the drums made it sound as if their enemies were surrounded by the Roadwarriors. Many were overcome with dread and gave up attempts of escape, which ensured the lack of stray victims escaping with supplies, and less competition against the great convoy.

  • Morale damage: +10% (morale_damage; raw value 0.1).

Roadwarrior Ambition

  • Land morale recovery speed: +10% (recover_army_morale_speed; raw value 0.1).
